newsitem.title: USA: Jones' lawyer accuses White House of smear campaign.
newsitem.headline: Jones' lawyer accuses White House of smear campaign.

text.p: A lawyer representing former Arkansas state employee Paula Jones in her sexual harassment case against President Bill Clinton on Friday accused the White House of orchestrating a smear campaign against him.

Attorney Gilbert Davis, one of two lawyers representing Jones, made the accusation after a Democratic political consultant released a video tape of him making risque remarks to a female client in a hotel room.

Davis, who is campaigning for a June 10 Republican primary for attorney general of Virginia, said the tape was old news. The incident took place in 1994 and the video first surfaced in January and was publicised at that time.

"It is no surprise that the president arrived back home from Europe early this morning and less than 24 hours later his attack dogs are again attempting to smear a representative of Paula Jones," said Davis.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry, asked about Davis' accusation, said: "I frankly don't know a thing about that."
Jones won a victory this week when the Supreme Court unanimously rejected Clinton's appeal to have her sexual harassment suit delayed until after he leaves office.
She alleged that then-Arkansas Gov. Clinton made unwanted sexual advances to her in a Little Rock hotel in 1991, including exposing himself to her and asking her to perform oral sex.
The video of Davis shows him in a hotel room with a woman called Ramona Hines. The video was shot by Hines' husband.

On the tape, Davis speaks about Hines' prospects of posing for Playboy. "I know what you want to do. You want to take your clothes off. You want to take all your clothes off and expose yourself," he says.
Davis said he did nothing wrong. "I have no apologies of anything I did," he said.
Hines tried to sell the tape to media outlets earlier this year but there were no buyers. She then gave it away and it received some publicity in Virginia.
Democratic consultant Jennifer Laszlo attempted to give the tape national coverage on Friday by calling a news conference. She said she had no current connection to the White House.
Davis dismissed this, saying he did not believe anything the White House said and he was the victim of a classic smear campaign.
